citing_sentence: Aspirin use after diagnosis is associated with improved lung cancer-specific survival.

cited_claimed.title: Metformin use and lung cancer survival: a population-based study in Norway

cited_abstract: We assessed associations between metformin use and survival in a nationwide Norwegian cohort of lung cancer (LC) patients. The study linked 22,324 LC patients from the Cancer Registry of Norway diagnosed 2005-2014 with the Norwegian Prescription Database. Post-diagnostic metformin use was associated with improved LCSS in all patients (HR = 0.83; 95%CI 0.73-0.95). Metformin use was associated with improved survival, especially LCSS in patients with regional stage SCC.

cited_sections.label: methods
cited_sections.title: Metformin and other variables
cited_sections.text: Use of metformin (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical code A10BA02), between January 2004 and December 2014, was separated into pre-diagnostic and post-diagnostic use.

cited_sections.label: methods
cited_sections.title: Study population
cited_sections.text: We identified 27,354 patients with primary LC diagnosis (Classification of Disease for Oncology, third edition (ICD-O-3) codes C33-C34), diagnosed from 01.01.2005 to 31.12.2014.

cited_sections.label: results
cited_sections.title: Post-diagnostic use
cited_sections.text: Post-diagnostic metformin use was associated with better survival in all patients (OS: HR = 0.87; 95%CI 0.77–0.98; LCSS: HR = 0.83; 95%CI 0.73–0.95; Table), SCC patients (LCSS: HR = 0.75; 95%CI 0.57–0.98), regional stage patients (LCSS: HR = 0.74; 95%CI 0.59–0.94), and regional stage SCC patients (OS: HR = 0.70; 95%CI 0.49–0.99, LSCC: HR = 0.57; 95%CI 0.38–0.86).

cited_sections.label: results
cited_sections.title: Follow-up
cited_sections.text: We followed 22,324 LC patients diagnosed from 2005–2014 until 30.06.2015 (median follow-up was 8.5 months); 16,928 deaths (75.7%) and 14,755 (66%) LC deaths were observed.
